patient_note_history:
History
HPI: A 26-year-old male complains of a cough for one week. His cough has been persistently productive with a small amount of white sputum, but there has been no hemoptysis. The cough has been associated with a mild fever and a sharp, stabbing pain in his right chest that is 8/10 in severity and exacerbated by cough and deep inspiration. Two weeks ago, he experienced a fever, rhinorrhea, and sore throat. He has no chills, night sweats, SOB, or wheezing. He has not experienced any weight or appetite changes nor does have any recent travel or TB exposure. 

ROS: Negative except as above.

Allergies: NKDA. 

Medications: Tylenol. 

PMH: He had Gonorrhea two years ago, which was treated with antibiotics. 

SH: He smokes 1 PPD since age 15; he drinks heavily on weekends but has a CAGE score of 0/4. He has had unprotected sex with multiple female partners.

FH: Noncontributory.

gold_additional_diagnosis:
• Pleurodynia: An uncommon acute illness usually caused by one of the coxsackieviruses. It occurs in summer and early fall and presents with acute, severe paroxysmal pain of the thorax or abdomen that worsens with cough or breathing. Most patients recover within 3 days to 1 week. 
• Other etiologies: Other causes of acute cough include aspiration (for which alcoholic, elderly, and neurologically impaired patients are at risk), pulmonary embolism (extremely rare in a young patient with no risk factors), and pulmonary edema (signs and symptoms of heart failure would be present). Given the patient's history, he should be screened for HIV infection. Notably, there is no evidence of immunosuppression on exam (e.g. no thrush), and in Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia, cough is usually nonproductive and accompanied by dyspnea.

Challenging Questions to Ask:
"Are antibiotics necessary for my recovery?"

Examinee Response:
"Possibly. Antibiotics are ineffective for bronchitis since this condition is mainly triggered by viruses that do not respond to these medications.. If I determine that you have bacterial pneumonia, treatment with antibiotics will be necessary.."

- The examinee asked the SP to list their concerns and listened to the response without interrupting.

Information Gathering:
- The examinee dictated data efficiently and accurately.

Sample Closure:

"Mr. Glenn, your cough is most likely due to an infection that can either be bacterial or viral. The chest pain you are feeling is likely caused by infection-related irritation of your lung membranes.. Some of this information can be more common with HIV, and given your sexual history, I recommend that we test for it. Another reason for your cough may be acid reflux, commonly known as heartburn. We are going to test your blood and sputum and obtain a chest x-ray to help us make a definitive diagnosis. If your cough is ongoing, we might also need to conduct a PPD test for tuberculosis.. In the meantime, I strongly recommend that you use condoms during intercourse to prevent STDs such as HIV and unwanted pregnancies. "Do you have any inquiries for me?"
